question: Find the paper on bromine substitution in lead-free CsSnI3 perovskite solar cells. Give its DOI and the reason the paper gives for the improved open-circuit voltage.
final_answer:
The paper investigating bromine substitution in lead-free $\text{CsSnI}_3$ perovskite solar cells has the DOI **10.1021/jp5126624** ("Impact of Anionic $\text{Br}^-$ Substitution on Open Circuit Voltage in Lead Free Perovskite ($\text{CsSnI}_{3-x}\text{Br}_x$) Solar Cells").

The paper gives the following reasons for the improved open-circuit voltage ($V_{oc}$):
1. Optical bandgap widening caused by Br doping/substitution.
2. A depreciating (reduced) background carrier concentration.
3. Increased resistance to charge recombination ($R_{rec}$) with higher Br content.

Short verbatim quotes from the paper:
- *"The high open circuit voltages derived by the widening of the band gap by Br doping/substitution is translated in terms of depreciating carrier concentration and increased resistance to charge recombination as revealed by impedance spectroscopy measurements."*
- *"Thus, the combination of band gap increment and reduced background carrier density resulting in suppressing charge recombination with higher Br - content lead to the attainment of higher $V_{\rm oc}$ (410 mV)."*
- *"The parallel resistance, attributed to a recombination resistance ($R_{\rm rec}$), increases for higher Br content (Figure 3b). Consequently, the $R_{\rm rec}$ of $\text{CsSnIBr}_2$ can explain the higher $V_{oc}$ obtained for this sample regardless of its lower $J_{sc}$."*
